## Human review verdict — chalbert/web-everything#1503

**Verdict:** ✅ pass — no blocking findings

### Panel verdicts

| lens | weight | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| correctness | mandatory | accept |

### Findings (1)

**test-coverage** (1)
- `src/_data/__tests__/backlogGraph.test.ts:108` — The regression test meant to guard `edges.sort(compareIds…)` is corpus-dependent and currently vacuous, so it does not actually defend the fix it claims to. — Mutation-verified: I reverted `edges.sort((a,b) => compareIds(a.from,b.from) || compareIds(a.to,b.to))` in src/_data/backlogGraph.js back to the pre-fix `Number(a.from) - Number(b.from) || Number(a.to) - Number(b.to))` (the exact NaN-comparator bug the PR's own commit message says was the round-2 finding) and reran the full backlogGraph.test.ts suite against the current live backlog corpus. All 7 tests, including the new 'applies that order to both nodes and edges' test, stayed GREEN — no named test reddens. The reason: the live backlog currently has zero hash-id items (`ls backlog | grep -E '^x'` is empty), so every edge pair is purely numeric and Number()-based comparison happens to agree with compareIds()-based comparison; the corpus-derived assertion has nothing to distinguish the two comparators. The sibling 'compareIds is a TOTAL order…' test does robustly defend the primitive itself (flipping its branch logic does redden it), but it never exercises whether buildGraph()'s edges.sort actually calls compareIds — so a future revert of just that one line, in a corpus state like today's, would ship silently. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: cosmetic]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Add a synthetic-fixture test that stubs loadBacklog() (or constructs a small in-memory item list) with explicit hash-id items carrying blockedBy edges to each other, so edges.sort's use of compareIds is exercised unconditionally rather than depending on what the live backlog happens to contain that day.

---

**Decision:** `accept` — recorded by operator.
**Lens:** `correctness` — a SINGLE-LENS run. One `judge` step, one juror, one lens; the table above lists only the lens that judged. The other 3 panel lenses (security, simplicity, standards-conformance) did NOT run and are not reported as unjudged.
Net basis: `0d10d3788e6808af409389164d9a697e5392bbb9..2dc4133190fb166020af8134f5209bfa3a035b93` (rev `origin/lane/slice-3007-phase2` at review time) — 4 net changed file(s) vs current main (#2450), not `gh pr diff`'s three-dot list.

_Recorded through the declared `review-pr` operation (#3035)._
